f.title: Report all USADRs in clinical research to HSA within the regulatory timelines
f.statement: Under the Health Products (Clinical Trials) Regulations and the Medicines (Clinical Trials) Regulations (and similar provisions in the clinical research materials regulations), sponsors are required to report unexpected serious adverse drug reactions (USADR) to HSA as soon as possible and in any case no later than the timelines stipulated in the regulations. Sponsors of any clinical research, including regulated clinical trials, must report to HSA all USADRs related to therapeutic products (TP), cell, tissue and gene therapy products (CTGTP) and medicinal products (MP) used in the research.
f.legal_basis: Health Products (Clinical Trials) Regulations; Medicines (Clinical Trials) Regulations; Health Products (Clinical Research Materials) Regulations; Medicines (Medicinal Products as Clinical Research Materials) Regulations
f.applicability: Clinical research in Singapore using TP, CTGTP or MP: regulated trials (CTA, CTN, CTC) and other clinical research (Section 1.3)
f.exceptions: Does not cover products with no ongoing clinical trial or other clinical research in Singapore.

rows.quote: In Singapore, sponsors are required, under the Health Products (Clinical Trials) Regulations and the Medicines (Clinical Trials) Regulations, to report USADR to HSA as soon as possible and in any case, no later than timelines stipulated in the regulations.

f.title: Keep reporting additional occurrences until the reference document is amended
f.statement: An unexpected adverse reaction is one whose nature or severity is not consistent with the relevant source document; until the source documents are amended, expedited reporting is required for additional occurrences of the reaction.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Until source documents are amended, expedited reporting is required for additional occurrences of the reaction.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: "is required" = Mandatory.

f.title: Use the IB or local product information as the reference for expectedness
f.statement: Expectedness is determined against: the Investigator's Brochure for a product not yet approved for marketing in Singapore; the local product information leaflet or the IB for a product approved in Singapore. Reports adding significant information on the specificity or severity of a known, documented serious ADR are unexpected events.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: (a) The Investigator’s Brochure will serve as the source document for a TP/CTGTP/MP that is not yet approved for marketing in Singapore; (b) The local product information leaflet or the Investigator’s Brochure for a TP/CTGTP/MP that has been approved for marketing in Singapore; (c) Reports which add significant information on specificity or severity of a known, already documented serious ADR constitute unexpected events.
rows.review_note: Review: definitional rule that decides reportability. Double-check: "will serve" read as binding; level debatable.

f.title: Apply medical judgement to treat important medical events as serious
f.statement: Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised in deciding whether expedited reporting is appropriate in other situations, such as important medical events that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation but may jeopardise the patient or require intervention to prevent a serious outcome; these should also usually be considered serious.
f.clause: 2.4 Serious Adverse Event or Adverse Drug Reaction - Seriousness

rows.quote: These should also usually be considered serious.
rows.location: 2.4 Serious Adverse Event or Adverse Drug Reaction - Seriousness
rows.review_note: Review: quote kept short because the sentence spans a page footer; statement paraphrases the preceding sentence. Double-check: statement wider than quote; should = Recommended.

f.title: Report all USADRs in ongoing Singapore research to IMNAD once minimum criteria are met; state the source
f.statement: All USADRs for pre-marketed (locally unregistered) and marketed (locally registered) TP/CTGTP/MP involved in ongoing clinical research in Singapore are subject to expedited reporting to the Investigational Medicines and Non-Clinical Assessments Division (IMNAD) when the minimum criteria are met. The source of each expedited safety report should always be specified.

rows.quote: Such expedited safety reports should be sent to the Investigational Medicines and Non-Clinical Assessments Division (IMNAD) when the minimum criteria for expedited reporting are met (refer to Section 3.2.3). The source of these expedited safety reports should always be specified.
rows.review_note: Review: level follows "should"; the underlying duty is statutory (see row 1). Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Unregistered IP: report local and overseas USADRs from all sources, including overseas spontaneous reports
f.statement: For locally unregistered TP/CTGTP/MP used as investigational product, all USADRs are subject to expedited reporting; safety reports should be submitted from any type of clinical investigation (including other protocols with the same product), from cases not reported directly to the sponsor (e.g. regulatory ADR registries), and overseas spontaneous reports meeting the minimum criteria.
f.clause: 3.1.1 Single Cases of USADR (a) Locally unregistered TP/CTGTP/MP used as investigational product
f.applicability: Locally unregistered products used as investigational product (usually CTA or CTC trials)
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote: Safety reports from the following sources should be submitted: • Any type of clinical investigation, independent of design or purpose (including other protocols with the same investigational TP/CTGTP/MP); • Cases not reported directly to a sponsor or manufacturer, for example, those found in regulatory authority-generated ADR registries; • Overseas spontaneous reports.
rows.location: 3.1.1 Single Cases of USADR (a) Locally unregistered TP/CTGTP/MP used as investigational product

f.title: Registered IP in regulated trials: test product local and overseas; comparator local only
f.statement: For regulated clinical trials on locally registered TP/CTGTP/MP: if the product is the test product, local and overseas USADR reports from the same protocol conducted in Singapore should be submitted; if it is the reference/comparator, only local USADR reports from the same protocol should be submitted. Additional information may be requested.
f.clause: 3.1.1 Single Cases of USADR (b) Locally registered TP/CTGTP/MP used as investigational product
f.applicability: Regulated clinical trials on locally registered products

rows.quote: If the locally registered TP/CTGTP/MP is used as a test product, local and overseas reports of USADR arising from that same clinical trial protocol conducted in Singapore should be submitted. • If the locally registered TP/CTGTP/MP is used as a reference (i.e., comparator), only local reports of USADR arising from that same clinical trial protocol should be submitted.
rows.location: 3.1.1 Single Cases of USADR (b) Locally registered TP/CTGTP/MP used as investigational product
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed (FAQ 7.1 table repeats this).

f.title: Registered IP in other clinical research: report local USADRs from the same protocol
f.statement: For other clinical research using a locally registered TP/CTGTP/MP as investigational product (e.g. observational trials), only local reports of USADR arising from the same protocol conducted in Singapore should be submitted.
f.clause: 3.1.1 Single Cases of USADR (b) Locally registered TP/CTGTP/MP used as investigational product
f.applicability: Other (non-regulated) clinical research with registered products

rows.quote: For other clinical research involving the use of locally registered TP/CTGTP/MP as investigational product (e.g., observational clinical trials of TP/CTGTP/MP), only local reports of USADR arising from that same clinical trial protocol conducted in Singapore should be submitted.
rows.location: 3.1.1 Single Cases of USADR (b) Locally registered TP/CTGTP/MP used as investigational product

f.title: Auxiliary products: report all local USADRs related to their use
f.statement: For regulated clinical trials and other clinical research, sponsors should submit to HSA all local USADRs related to the use of an auxiliary TP/MP in the research protocol, regardless of the registration status of the auxiliary product.
f.clause: 3.1.1 Single Cases of USADR (c) TP/MP used as auxiliary product
f.applicability: Auxiliary products (used per protocol but not as investigational product)

rows.quote: For regulated clinical trials and other clinical research, sponsors should submit to HSA all local USADR that are related to the use of the auxiliary TP/MP in that research protocol. This is regardless of the registration status of the auxiliary TP/MP.
rows.location: 3.1.1 Single Cases of USADR (c) TP/MP used as auxiliary product

f.title: No expedited reporting for expected, unrelated, non-serious or placebo events
f.statement: Expedited reporting is ordinarily not required for: serious but expected AEs/ADRs; serious adverse events considered not related to the study product, expected or not; non-serious ADRs, expected or not; adverse events associated with placebo.

rows.quote: It should be noted that expedited reporting in the following situations would ordinarily not be required: • Adverse events or adverse drug reactions which are serious but expected • Serious adverse events from clinical investigations that are considered not related to study product, whether expected or not • Non-serious adverse drug reactions, whether expected or not • Adverse events associated with placebo
rows.review_note: Review: exemption list recorded as Permitted. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Perform causality assessment; a reasonable possibility by reporter or sponsor makes the case an ADR
f.statement: Causality assessment is required for clinical investigation cases. All cases judged by either the reporting healthcare professional or the sponsor as having a reasonable suspected causal relationship to the product qualify as ADRs.

rows.quote: Causality assessment is required for clinical investigation cases. All cases judged by either the reporting health care professional or the sponsor as having a reasonable suspected causal relationship to the TP/CTGTP/MP qualify as ADRs.

f.title: Submit spontaneous reports lacking detail only after causality assessment
f.statement: If a spontaneous report initially lacks sufficient detail to permit rational causality assessment by the healthcare professional or sponsor, the report (even if serious) may be submitted to HSA only after proper causality assessment has been made by a healthcare professional or the sponsor based on updated information.

rows.quote: However, for the purposes of regulatory reporting, if a spontaneous report initially lacks sufficient detail to permit rational assessment of causality by the healthcare professional or sponsor, the report (even if serious in nature), may be submitted to HSA only after proper causality assessment has been made by a healthcare professional or the sponsor based on updated information.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: may = Permitted.

f.title: Rapidly communicate other observations that may change the benefit-risk or trial conduct
f.statement: Beyond single cases, information that might materially influence the benefit-risk assessment of a product or be sufficient to consider changes in its administration or in the overall conduct of a clinical investigation may necessitate rapid communication to IMNAD, applying medical and scientific judgement. Examples: a clinically important increase in the rate of an expected serious ADR; a significant hazard such as lack of efficacy in treating life-threatening disease; a major safety finding from a newly completed animal study (e.g. carcinogenicity).

rows.quote: There are situations in addition to single case reports of “serious” adverse events or reactions that may necessitate rapid communication to the Investigational Medicines and Non-Clinical Assessments Division; appropriate medical and scientific judgement should be applied for each situation.
rows.review_note: Review: examples (a)-(c) paraphrased in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Notify IMNAD of fatal or life-threatening USADRs within 7 calendar days
f.statement: Fatal or life-threatening USADRs occurring in clinical investigations qualify for very rapid reporting: IMNAD should be notified as soon as possible but no later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor that a case qualifies.
f.legal_basis: Health Products (Clinical Trials) Regulations; Medicines (Clinical Trials) Regulations; Health Products (Clinical Research Materials) Regulations; Medicines (Medicinal Products as Clinical Research Materials) Regulations

rows.deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge
rows.quote: The Investigational Medicines and Non-Clinical Assessments Division should be notified as soon as possible but no later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor that a case qualifies,
rows.review_note: Review: level Mandatory although the passage says "should": Section 1.2 states the timelines are required by the clinical trials regulations. Double-check: accepted; confidence reduced for the modal mismatch.

deadline_rule.clock_start: first knowledge by the sponsor that a case qualifies

f.title: Follow with as complete a report as possible within 8 additional calendar days
f.statement: The 7-day notification of a fatal or life-threatening USADR should be followed by as complete a report as possible within 8 additional calendar days; it may include an assessment of the importance and implication of the findings, including relevant previous experience with the same or similar products. Subsequent follow-up reports should be submitted as information becomes available.
f.legal_basis: Health Products (Clinical Trials) Regulations; Medicines (Clinical Trials) Regulations; Health Products (Clinical Research Materials) Regulations; Medicines (Medicinal Products as Clinical Research Materials) Regulations

rows.deadline: Within 8 additional calendar days after the 7-day notification; later follow-ups as available
rows.quote: followed by as complete a report as possible within 8 additional calendar days.

deadline_rule.clock_start: 7 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor that a case qualifies

f.title: File other USADRs within 15 calendar days of meeting the minimum criteria
f.statement: USADRs that are not fatal or life-threatening must be filed as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor that the case meets the minimum criteria for expedited reporting. Follow-up reports should be submitted as information becomes available.
f.legal_basis: Health Products (Clinical Trials) Regulations; Medicines (Clinical Trials) Regulations; Health Products (Clinical Research Materials) Regulations; Medicines (Medicinal Products as Clinical Research Materials) Regulations

rows.deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 15 calendar days after first knowledge
rows.quote: USADRs that are not fatal or life-threatening must be filed as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor that the case meets the minimum criteria for expedited reporting. Follow-up reports should be submitted as it becomes available.

deadline_rule.clock_start: first knowledge by the sponsor that the case meets the minimum criteria for expedited reporting
deadline_rule.applies_to: USADRs that are not fatal or life-threatening

f.title: Submit initial reports once the five minimum criteria are met; actively seek follow-up
f.statement: Initial reports should be submitted as soon as possible and within the prescribed time as long as the minimum criteria are met: an identifiable patient; a suspect product; an identifiable reporting source; an event or outcome identifiable as serious and unexpected; a reasonable suspected causal relationship. Follow-up information should be actively sought and submitted as it becomes available.
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote: Nevertheless, for regulatory purposes, initial reports should be submitted as soon as possible and within the prescribed time, as long as the following minimum criteria are met: • An identifiable patient; • A suspect TP/CTGTP/MP; • An identifiable reporting source; • Event or outcome that can be identified as serious and unexpected; • There is a reasonable suspected causal relationship. Follow-up information should be actively sought and submitted as it becomes available.

f.title: Include the Appendix 2 data elements in expedited reports (CIOMS-I accepted)
f.statement: The CIOMS-I form is a widely accepted standard for expedited reporting; whatever form or format is used, the data elements in Appendix 2 should, when available, be included in any expedited report (some items may not be relevant).

rows.quote: However, no matter what the form or format used, it is important that certain data elements described in Appendix 2, when available, be included in any expedited report (although some items may not be relevant depending on the circumstances).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: "it is important" = Recommended.

f.title: Code USADR descriptions with MedDRA
f.statement: It is recommended that USADR descriptions be reported using MedDRA.

rows.quote: It is recommended that the description for the USADRs be reported using MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities),

f.title: Send reports to IMNAD and other official parties such as investigators and IRBs
f.statement: All reports must be sent to IMNAD and to other official parties requiring them (e.g. investigators and institutional review boards).

rows.quote: All reports must be sent to the Investigational Medicines and Non-Clinical Assessments Division, and other official parties requiring them (e.g., Investigators and Institutional Review Boards).

f.title: Regulated trials: submit expedited reports through the PRISM ESR module
f.statement: For regulated trials, expedited safety reports should be submitted through the Expedited Safety Reporting (ESR) online module in the Pharmaceutical Regulatory Information System (PRISM).

rows.quote: For regulated trials, the expedited safety reports should be submitted through the Expedited Safety Reporting (ESR) online module in Pharmaceutical Regulatory Information System (PRISM).

f.title: Other clinical research: submit expedited reports to HSA by email
f.statement: For other (non-regulated) clinical research, expedited safety reports should be submitted to HSA by email (dedicated clinical-trial SAE mailbox).

rows.quote: For other clinical research, the expedited safety reports should be submitted via email to
rows.review_note: Review: quote stops before the e-mail address. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Break the blind only for the specific patient when a case is reportable
f.statement: When a serious adverse reaction is judged reportable on an expedited basis, it is recommended that the sponsor break the blind only for that specific patient, even if the investigator has not; when possible and appropriate, the blind should be maintained for those responsible for analysis and interpretation of results (e.g. biometrics personnel).
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote: Although it is advantageous to retain the blind for all patients prior to final study analysis, when a serious adverse reaction is judged reportable on an expedited basis, it is recommended that the blind be broken only for that specific patient by the sponsor even if the investigator has not broken the blind. It is also recommended that, when possible and appropriate, the blind be maintained for those persons, such as biometrics personnel, responsible for analysis and interpretation of results at the study’s conclusion.

f.title: Submit unblinding information given to other authorities through the ESR form
f.statement: For events where the treatment blind has been broken for submission to the EMA or other national authorities, this information should be submitted through the online ESR form.

rows.quote: For events where the treatment blind has been broken for submission to the European Medicines Agency (EMEA) or other national authorities, this information should be submitted through the online ESR form.

f.title: Placebo revealed before reporting: no expedited report needed; after reporting: update IMNAD
f.statement: If the blind is broken and reveals placebo and no expedited report has been filed to IMNAD yet, expedited reporting is not required. If a report has already been submitted and the blind is subsequently broken, IMNAD must be updated by sending the safety report highlighting the new information so the database can be updated.
f.exceptions: Placebo revealed before any expedited report was filed: expedited reporting not required.

rows.quote: On the other hand, if a report has already been submitted and subsequently, the blind is broken, the IMNAD must be updated on this new information by sending the safety report and highlighting this information for the database to be updated.
rows.review_note: Review: the placebo exemption kept as an exception of this row. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Agree in advance with IMNAD on disease-related events when serious outcomes are efficacy endpoints
f.statement: When a fatal or other serious outcome is the primary efficacy endpoint and breaking the blind could compromise the investigation, it may be appropriate to reach agreement with IMNAD in advance on serious events to be treated as disease-related and not subject to routine expedited reporting.

rows.quote: Under these and similar circumstances, it may be appropriate to reach agreement with the IMNAD in advance concerning serious events that would be treated as disease-related and not subjected to routine expedited reporting.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: may = Permitted.

f.title: Cross-reference expedited ADRs across all presentations and uses of the product
f.statement: An ADR that qualifies for expedited reporting with one presentation (dosage form, formulation, delivery system) or use (indication, population) of a product should be reported or referenced to regulatory filings across the other presentations and uses; it is recommended to cross-reference such ADRs to regulatory records for all other dosage forms and uses.
f.clause: 5.1 Products with More Than One Presentation or Use

rows.quote: To avoid ambiguities and uncertainties, an ADR that qualifies for expedited reporting with one presentation of a product (e.g., a dosage form, formulation, delivery system) or product use (e.g., for an indication or population), should be reported or referenced to regulatory filings across other product presentations and uses.
rows.location: 5.1 Products with More Than One Presentation or Use

f.title: Treat post-study SAEs reported by investigators as study reports
f.statement: Serious adverse events occurring after a patient has completed a study (including protocol-required post-treatment follow-up) that are reported by an investigator should be regarded as study reports for expedited reporting; causality and expectedness must be assessed to decide whether expedited reporting is required.
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote: Such cases should be regarded for expedited reporting purposes as though they were study reports. Therefore, causality assessment and determination of expectedness are needed for a decision on whether or not expedited reporting is required.

f.title: Keep the Investigator's Brochure safety information updated; follow IRB reporting rules
f.statement: The sponsor should amend the Investigator's Brochure as needed to keep the description of safety information updated, and should refer to the current safety reporting requirements of the IRB.
f.clause: 6. Informing Investigators and EC/IRB of New Safety Information

rows.quote: In general, the sponsor of a study should amend the Investigator’s Brochure as needed, so as to keep the description of safety information updated. Sponsors should refer to the current safety reporting requirements of the IRB.
rows.location: 6. Informing Investigators and EC/IRB of New Safety Information

f.title: Start submitting USADRs upon trial authorisation, notification acceptance or certificate
f.statement: Submission of USADRs should start immediately upon clinical trial authorisation, acceptance of notification or issuance of a clinical trial certificate.
f.clause: 7. FAQs, 7.2 When should the sponsor start or stop submitting USADR to HSA?

rows.quote: Submission of USADR should start immediately upon clinical trial authorisation, acceptance of notification or issuance of a clinical trial certificate.
rows.location: 7. FAQs, 7.2 When should the sponsor start or stop submitting USADR to HSA?

f.title: Communicate new safety concerns arising during the CTA review period promptly by email
f.statement: If any new safety concern surfaces from individual reports or aggregate analysis of USADRs during the clinical trial application review period, the local sponsor should ensure that the new safety information is promptly communicated to HSA by email for the benefit-risk assessment of the trial.
f.clause: 7. FAQs, 7.2 When should the sponsor start or stop submitting USADR to HSA?

rows.quote: However, should any new safety concern surface from individual reports or aggregate analysis of USADR during the clinical trial application review period, the local sponsor should ensure that the new safety information is promptly communicated to HSA by email so that the information can be considered in the benefit-risk assessment of the clinical trial.
rows.location: 7. FAQs, 7.2 When should the sponsor start or stop submitting USADR to HSA?

f.title: Stop USADR submissions at LPLV, but report later relevant safety information
f.statement: Submission of USADR reports may stop when Last Patient Last Visit (LPLV) is reached in Singapore, unless otherwise indicated in the protocol. The local sponsor should nevertheless inform HSA of any new safety information emerging thereafter, particularly if relevant to previously treated trial participants.
f.clause: 7. FAQs, 7.2 When should the sponsor start or stop submitting USADR to HSA?

rows.quote: Submission of USADR reports may stop when Last Patient Last Visit (LPLV) is achieved in Singapore, unless otherwise indicated in the protocol. However, the local sponsor should inform HSA of any new safety information that emerges thereafter, particularly if the information were of relevance or potential significance to previously-treated trial participants.
rows.location: 7. FAQs, 7.2 When should the sponsor start or stop submitting USADR to HSA?
rows.review_note: Review: headline duty (inform after LPLV) is "should"; stop is "may". Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Compassionate use under a CTA/CTC: submit USADRs to IMNAD
f.statement: If a compassionate use programme takes the form of a long-term clinical trial extension protocol with a CTA or CTC, USADRs should be submitted to IMNAD in accordance with the clinical trial regulations and guidance.
f.clause: 7. FAQs, 7.3 Named Patient Programme / compassionate use
f.applicability: Compassionate use as a CTA/CTC extension protocol

rows.quote: If the compassionate use programme takes the form of a long-term clinical trial extension protocol for which a CTA or CTC has been granted, USADR should be submitted to the Investigational Medicines and Non-Clinical Assessments Division, in accordance with clinical trial regulations and guidance.
rows.location: 7. FAQs, 7.3 Named Patient Programme / compassionate use

f.title: Other compassionate use: submit all local serious ADRs to the Vigilance & Compliance Division
f.statement: All local reports of serious ADRs (regardless of expectedness) arising from the use of unregistered drugs in other compassionate use programmes (without a CTA or CTC) should be submitted to HSA's Vigilance & Compliance Division.
f.clause: 7. FAQs, 7.3 Named Patient Programme / compassionate use
f.applicability: Compassionate use / named patient programmes of unregistered drugs without CTA or CTC

rows.quote: All local reports of serious adverse drug reactions (regardless of expectedness) arising from the use of unregistered drugs in other types of compassionate use programmes (i.e., those without a CTA or CTC) should be submitted to the Vigilance & Compliance Division of HSA.
rows.location: 7. FAQs, 7.3 Named Patient Programme / compassionate use

f.title: No routine DSUR or periodic line listing submission; submit if HSA requests
f.statement: There is currently no requirement to submit periodic line listings, DSURs, annual or periodic safety reports to HSA; they may be submitted at the sponsor's discretion, and HSA may request them when deemed necessary.
f.clause: 7. FAQs, 7.4 Periodic line listings, DSUR, annual or periodic safety reports

rows.quote: There is currently no requirement for submission of such reports. These reports may be submitted to HSA at the sponsor’s discretion. HSA may also request for these reports to be submitted when deemed necessary.
rows.location: 7. FAQs, 7.4 Periodic line listings, DSUR, annual or periodic safety reports

f.title: Procedure-related SAEs: inform HSA by email when a product or device may have contributed
f.statement: Procedure-related SAEs generally need not be reported to HSA. However, if the procedure involves a TP, CTGTP, MP or medical device that might have contributed to the event, with potential to affect the safety of other participants, and preventive actions can be taken at local sites, HSA should be informed by email, as a protocol or informed consent amendment may be warranted.
f.exceptions: Procedure-related SAEs in general need not be reported.

rows.quote: However, if the procedure involves the use of a TP, CTGTP, MP or medical device that might have contributed to the adverse event which has the potential to affect the safety and welfare of other trial participants, and preventive actions can be taken at local trial sites to prevent a similar occurrence, HSA should be informed by email since such an event might warrant a protocol or informed consent form amendment.

f.title: Expected serious reactions may be reported when they affect benefit-risk or trial conduct
f.statement: Expected reactions can be reported when the information may materially influence the benefit-risk assessment of a product or the overall conduct of a clinical trial, e.g. a clinically important increase in the rate of a serious expected ADR.

rows.quote: Expected reactions can be reported when the information may materially influence a) the benefit-risk assessment of a product, or b) the overall conduct of a clinical trial

f.title: Start the USADR clock at first receipt by the sponsor anywhere
f.statement: The reporting timeline for USADR submission starts upon first receipt by the sponsor, regardless of physical location.

rows.quote: The reporting timeline starts upon first receipt by the sponsor, regardless of physical location.

f.title: Avoid batch submission of USADRs unless the legal timeline is not compromised
f.statement: Sponsors must submit USADR reports as soon as possible (without undue delay); batch reporting is generally not encouraged and should be considered only if the sponsor can ensure the legal obligation is not compromised.

rows.quote: encouraged and should be considered only if the sponsor is able to ensure that the legal obligation is not compromised.

f.title: Local sponsor keeps overall responsibility for safety reporting even when delegated to a CRO
f.statement: All clinical trials conducted in Singapore require a local sponsor, who assumes responsibility for ensuring that safety reporting complies with local requirements. Safety reporting submissions may be contractually delegated to a CRO, but the local sponsor keeps overall responsibility.

f.statement: The local sponsor may give a CRO drafter rights for the ESR module so the CRO drafts ESR applications and notifies the sponsor to submit; giving a CRO submitter rights lets it view and access all clinical trial applications filed under the sponsor company.

f.title: Use the same sponsor case identification number for initial and follow-up reports
f.statement: The sponsor/manufacturer's identification number for the case must be the same for the initial and follow-up reports on the same case; reports should also carry the HSA clinical trial application/reference number.
f.clause: 9.2 Appendix 2: Data Elements, 6. Administrative and Sponsor/Company Details
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Data integrity & records

f.title: Investigator supplies additional requested information on deaths to HSA, IRB and sponsor
